title: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid I (ACSF.I)

steps_raw.instruction: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid I (ACSF.I)

Scope and Applicability: Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid I (ACSF.I) is used for applications including transcardial perfusion prior to fresh mouse brain slicing and as a bathing solution during fresh mouse brain slicing.

10 mM Magnesium Sulfate, Heptahydrate
1.25 mM Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate
2.5 mM Potassium Chloride
5 mM Sodium L-Ascorbate
25 mM Sodium Bicarbonate
96 mM N-Methyl-D-glucamine
12 mM N-Acetyl-L-cysteine
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Prepare working stocks of reagents, as necessary. Label the stock bottles with contents, preparer’s initials, preparation date, storage requirement and expiration date.

200 mM Calcium Chloride, dihydrate: Prepare a 200 mM stock solution by dissolving 29.4 g of CaCl2·2 H2O in 1 Liter of MilliQ Water in a labeled 1 Liter polystyrene bottle. Store the stock solution at room temperature for up to 60 days.

1 M HEPES: Prepare a 1M stock solution by dissolving 238.3 g of HEPES in 1 Liter of MilliQ Water in a labeled 1 Liter polystyrene bottle. Store the stock solution at room temperature for up to 60 days.

1 M Magnesium Sulfate, heptahydrate: Prepare a 1 M stock solution by dissolving 246 g of MgSO4.7 H2O 1 M in 1 Liter of MilliQ Water in a labeled 1 Liter polystyrene bottle. Store the stock solution at room temperature for up to 60 days.
250 mM Potassium Chloride, 125 mM Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate, 100 mM Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate solution.
Prepare a 250 mM stock solution of Potassium Chloride by dissolving 18.6 g of KCl in 1 Liter of MilliQ Water in a labeled 1 Liter polystyrene bottle.
Add 17.3 g of NaH2PO4 to the Potassium Chloride solution.
Add 24.6 g of MgSO4.7 H2O to the Potassium Chloride / Sodium Phosphate Solution.
Store the stock solution at room temperature for up to 60 days.

Sodium Pyruvate: Prepare a 500 mM stock solution by dissolving 55 g of CH3COCOONa in 1 Liter of MilliQ Water in a labeled 1 Liter polystyrene bottle. Store the stock solution at 4°C for up to 60 days.
Taurine: Prepare a 100 mM stock solution by dissolving 0.625 g of Taurine in 50 ml of MilliQ Water in a labeled 50 ml conical tube. Store the stock solution at 4°C for up to 60 days.

Thiourea: Prepare a 1.6 M stock solution by dissolving 6.08 g of Thiourea in 50 ml of MilliQ Water. Aliquot 1.4 ml the solution into each of 35 labeled 1.7 ml microcentrifuge tubes. Store the aliquots at -20°C for up to 60 days. The solution must be warmed to room temperature prior to use.
Label a sterile 1 liter polystyrene bottle with the reagent name, date and the preparer’s initials.
Obtain a stir bar and place it in the container.
Set up the stir plate in the fume hood.
Methodology/Procedures (record all lot numbers and volumes used in the appropriate reagent preparation notebook):
Consult the reagent request form to determine the volume of ACSF.I to prepare. Table 1 lists the reagent quantities required to make either 500 ml or 1 Liter of ACSF.I.
To make 1000 ml of Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid.I (ACSF.I):
Using a graduated cylinder, measure 500 ml of MilliQ Water. Add the water to an appropriately labeled container containing a stir bar.
Place the container on a stir plate and begin stirring at a high setting (7 or higher).
Using a sterile serological pipette or graduated cylinder, add 20 ml of the 1 M HEPES stock solution.
Using a sterile serological pipette, add 10 ml of the 250 mM Potassium Chloride, 125 mM Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate, 100 mM Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate solution.
Using a sterile serological pipette, add 6 ml of the 500 mM Sodium Pyruvate stock solution.
Using a P200 Pipetteman and a P200 pipette tip, add 100 µl of the 100 mM Taurine stock solution.
Using a sterile serological pipette, add 1.25 ml of the 1.6 M Thiourea stock solution. Note: the solution must be at room temperature to fully dissolve.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 4.51 g of D-Glucose. Slowly add weighed D-Glucose to the container while stirring.
Weigh out 540 mg of Myo inositol. Slowly add weighed Myo inositol to the container while stirring.
Weigh out 1.96 g of N-Acetyl-L-cysteine. Slowly add weighed N-Acetyl-L-cysteine to the container while stirring.
Weigh out 19.4 g of N-Methyl-d-glucamide. Slowly add weighed N-Methyl-d-glucamide to the container while stirring.
Weigh out 1.0 g of Sodium L-Ascorbate. Slowly add weighed Sodium L-Ascorbate to the container while stirring.
Weigh out 2.1 g of Sodium Bicarbonate. Slowly add weighed Sodium Bicarbonate to the container while stirring.
Continue stirring at a high speed (setting 7 or higher) until all of the chemicals are fully in solution.
Using a calibrated pH meter, measure the pH of the ACSF solution. Adjust the pH to 7.3 by adding 5 N HCl dropwise. Up to 16 ml of HCl may be needed to reach the desired pH.
Using a sterile serological pipette, add 2.5 ml of the 200 mM Calcium Chloride stock solution.
Using a sterile serological pipette, add 9 ml of the 1 M Magnesium Sulfate stock solution.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Adjust final volume to 1000 ml with MilliQ Water using the graduation marks on the side of the container (if calibrated) or a graduated cylinder.
Measure the osmolarity of a 10 µl sample of the solution using an osmometer. If the osmolarity is not 300-310 mOsm (295-305 mmol/kg), adjust as needed.
If the osmolarity is too high, add MilliQ water.
If the osmolarity is too low, add a volume (X) of 1 mg/ml NaCl solution determined by the following equation
O= observed osmolarity
X=volume of 1 mg/ml NaCl solution to add (in ml)
Confirm that the correct osmolarity has been reached after addition of NaCl or water.
Filter the ACSF through a Corning 1 liter 0.45 µm filter system.
Using Tygon tubing, attach the Corning filter system to the Gast vacuum pump. Turn on the pump.
Filter 500 ml at a time, stirring the remaining ACSF constantly on a stir plate.
Label the bottle with reagent name, date, time and preparer’s initials. ACSF expires one week from date of preparation.
Record the date of preparation, lot numbers of all components and osmolarity in the reagent preparation notebook.
Dispose of excess reagent directly into municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with MilliQ Water.

Rinse all beakers, graduated cylinders, and other equipment used to prepare ACSF solutions with MilliQ Water only (No Detergent). Invert all beakers and graduated cylinders and leave on clean absorbent pad to air dry.
Technical Information:
Artificial Cerebrospinal Fluid (ACSF) must be made fresh the day it is to be used. Store at 4°C until use.
Use within one week from the day it is made, or at the discretion of the investigator.

The Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate is added to the solution twice; first as a 1 M stock and then again as part of the stock solution of Potassium Chloride/ Sodium Phosphate monobasic monohydrate/ Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate. The 1 M stock is used to bring the Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate concentration up to the final desired level of 10 mM.

The osmolarity of the ACSF normally should not need to be adjusted if all of the components were added correctly. If the osmolarity does need to be adjusted, add MilliQ Water to lower or Sodium Chloride to raise the value.
